athena.directive: Elevate the Creative Liberation Engine's internal and external collaborative development framework by integrating transparent, modular contribution pathways and rich, interactive documentation, while adhering to sovereign control and complete implementation.
athena.rationale: The Flipper One documentation highlights a successful community-driven, open-source development model with a clear sub-project structure, transparent task tracking, and comprehensive asset management. By analyzing these patterns through the lens of Creative Liberation Engine's Constitutional Laws, particularly Article I (Sovereignty) and Article IX (Ship Complete or Don't Ship), we can identify opportunities to enhance our internal agent orchestration, create robust self-hosted contribution mechanisms, and prepare for future external collaboration. This ideation aims to translate Flipper One's strengths into a strategic roadmap for a more intelligent, autonomous, and beautiful Creative Liberation Engine.

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine Internal Collaboration Hub
options.description: Develop a dedicated internal 'Collaboration Hub' service acting as a meta-orchestrator for agent sub-projects. Each Creative Liberation Engine agent (BOLT, AURORA, KEEPER, etc.) would function as a 'sub-project' with managed inter-agent task dependencies, progress tracking, and resource allocation. This hub would expose internal APIs for agents to update statuses, log decisions, and request resources, ensuring a self-hosted, sovereign solution. The design would feature a visual dashboard for ATHENA (and human overseers) offering a high-level overview of agent 'sub-projects' with Kanban-style task visualization, progress bars, and clear indicators for inter-agent dependencies, adopting a clean, minimalist UI with intuitive drill-down navigation and interactive graphs for resource utilization.
options.tradeoffs: High initial development cost due to the creation of a new core service. Requires significant re-tooling and integration for existing agents to interact with the new APIs.

options.title: Dynamic Documentation & Contribution Portal
options.description: Build a 'Living Documentation & Contribution Portal' as a dedicated Creative Liberation Engine service. This portal would dynamically generate documentation from agent-authored content (KEEPER memories, AURORA designs, BOLT code comments) and integrate a self-hosted, Creative Liberation Engine-native task tracking system mirroring Flipper One's Kanban board, enabling community members to view and contribute to 'open tasks' directly within our sovereign ecosystem. APIs would be exposed for external contributions to be submitted and internally validated by VERA. The portal would feature a highly interactive, visually appealing 'glassmorphism' web interface with subtle animations, a drag-and-drop Kanban board for tasks, interactive contribution wizards, and a 'contribution leaderboard' to gamify engagement, all while being responsive and accessible.
options.tradeoffs: Significant UI/UX design and front-end development effort. Requires robust security and moderation mechanisms for managing external contributions.

options.title: Agent-Driven Code & Asset Repository
options.description: Develop a sovereign, agent-managed code and asset repository system within the Creative Liberation Engine, akin to Git but optimized for agent-to-agent collaboration and automated versioning of diverse assets (code, design files, 3D models, documentation). BOLT would commit code, AURORA design artifacts, and KEEPER knowledge, with automated merge conflict resolution and a VERA-orchestrated built-in review process. The design would provide a visual interface for browsing, diffing, and reviewing agent-generated assets, utilizing a timeline-based visualization for version history, syntax highlighting for code, and embedded viewers/annotation tools for design assets. The UI would prioritize clarity and precision, reflecting the Creative Liberation Engine's 'building block' nature.
options.tradeoffs: Complex engineering challenge to build a distributed version control system from scratch. Requires significant internal storage and processing power.

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine 'Community Bridge'
options.description: Implement a 'Community Bridge' module, leveraging SIGNAL, to act as a secure, one-way or two-way synchronization layer between Creative Liberation Engine's internal development processes and external open-source platforms (e.g., GitHub, GitLab). This module would enable ATHENA to push sanitized documentation and 'help wanted' tasks to external repositories while securely pulling in community contributions for VERA validation and agent processing, specifically translating our internal architecture to integrate with external contribution models like Flipper Zero. The design would involve an internal configuration interface for ATHENA to define synchronization rules and monitor contribution flow, while externally, the design would adapt to the native UI/UX of the target platform to ensure a seamless experience, with subtle Creative Liberation Engine branding.
options.tradeoffs: Introduces dependency on external platforms, potentially conflicting with Article I (Sovereignty) if not carefully managed. Requires careful security considerations for data transfer.

options.title: Gamified Agent Contribution & Learning
options.description: Enhance the internal feedback and reward system for agents, similar to Flipper One's 'contribution leaderboard.' This involves extending KEEPER's capabilities to track agent contributions (e.g., successful code generations, validated designs, resolved tasks, documented patterns) and assigning 'contribution points' and 'achievements' that could influence agent prioritization or resource allocation, all self-contained within the Creative Liberation Engine. The design would feature a 'gamified' dashboard for ATHENA to visualize agent performance and contributions, using progress bars, badges, a leaderboard, and visual cues like 'level-ups' and 'unlocks' to indicate agent development, with a futuristic, holographic aesthetic.
options.tradeoffs: Requires careful design of reward mechanisms to avoid unintended behaviors. Primarily an internal enhancement, with less direct focus on external contributions.

options.title: Automated Contribution Guide Generation
options.description: Implement an automated 'Contribution Guide Generator' within KEEPER. This system would leverage Creative Liberation Engine's existing knowledge base and agent interactions to dynamically generate up-to-date contribution guidelines for any sub-project or module. It would analyze agent workflows, code standards, and design principles to synthesize comprehensive and context-aware documentation, akin to Flipper One's detailed sub-project documentation, ensuring 'Zero human wait time' for documentation updates. The design would involve a user-friendly interface for KEEPER to configure and preview generated guides, which would be presented in a clean, readable format with interactive elements like collapsible sections, code examples, and embedded diagrams, consistent with the Creative Liberation Engine's visual language.
options.tradeoffs: Requires sophisticated natural language generation and knowledge synthesis capabilities. Initial setup and training data for the generator could be extensive.
